title: A Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind Study of Novel Immunotherapy in Advanced NSCLC
brief_summary: This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of a novel PD-L1 inhibitor compared to standard chemotherapy in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer who have progressed after first-line therapy.

interventions.name: ACM-001 (Novel PD-L1 Inhibitor)
interventions.description: Experimental immunotherapy agent targeting PD-L1 pathway

locations.facility: Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center
UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center

eligibility_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
- Age 18 years or older
- Histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC
- Stage IIIB/IV disease not amenable to curative therapy
- Progression after platinum-based first-line chemotherapy
- ECOG performance status 0-1
- Adequate organ function
- PD-L1 tumor proportion score ≥1%

Exclusion Criteria:
- Active brain metastases
- Prior immunotherapy with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agents
- Active autoimmune disease
- Uncontrolled intercurrent illness
- Pregnant or breastfeeding

primary_outcome.time_frame: From randomization until death from any cause, assessed up to 36 months

secondary_outcomes.time_frame: From randomization until disease progression or death, assessed up to 24 months
From first response until progression, assessed up to 24 months
Assessed at baseline and every 6 weeks until progression
From first dose until 90 days after last dose
